approach.statement_refutation: StatementRefutation.lean: the D7 statement-level existence statements are refuted as formalized. Counterexample spacetime on PUnit: volume = Dirac, laplacian = LinearMap.id, timeDerivative = 0, dist = 0, dim = 0, certified IsClosedRiemannianManifold (the predicate does not mention the operators). General schema: any nonempty HeatSpacetime with laplacian = id and timeDerivative = 0 admits no IsHeatKernel/IsHeatKernelV1 kernel (solves forces K = 0 vs positive). Consequence: D7-HEAT-KERNEL-EXISTENCE cannot be closed by proving the statement as written; the statement must be repaired by pinning the operators to geometric ones (data-level HeatKernelDataV1 is the honest target).

approach.geometric_repair: GeometricRepair.lean: (1) AnnihilatesConstants S := (S.laplacian 1 = 0) — the one geometric necessary condition expressible over the schematic interface and verifiable for the honest flat operator (flatHeatSpacetime_laplacian_one); it excludes the refuting spacetime (laplacian = id) and is strictly stronger than IsClosedRiemannianManifold; models: punitDiracSpacetime (zero operators, Dirac volume) and adversarialTimeDerivativeSpacetime. The stronger classical conditions (self-adjointness, dissipativity) are deliberately NOT fields: their all-functions Bochner-integral forms are false for the honest packaged flat Laplacian (informal counterexample u = 1, v = log cosh on ℝ: ∫1·Δv = [tanh] = 2 ≠ 0 = ∫Δ1·v), and their C_c/C² forms need a smooth normed structure the interface does not carry. (2) Second statement-level refutation: adversarialTimeDerivativeSpacetime (volume = Dirac, Δ = 0, ∂_t = id, dist = 0, dim = 0) satisfies both predicates and admits no IsHeatKernelV1 witness; not_forall_annihilatesConstants_implies_exists_snapshot_kernel. (3) Time-rescaling: flatSnapshotSpacetime (∂_t := Δ) makes the solves field vacuous; flatKernelRescaled n c (x,y,t) ↦ flatKernel n x y (c·t) satisfies IsHeatKernelV1 for every c > 0 but for c = 2 fails the PDE at x = y = 0, t = 1 (chain rule gives 2·ΔK(·,0,2) vs the required ΔK(·,0,2), and ΔK(0,0,2) = K(0,0,2)·(-n/4) ≠ 0); hence not_forall_isHeatKernelV1_imp_isHeatKernelPDE and snapshot_pde_predicates_incomparable (with the converse from PDERepair). (4) HeatKernelExistenceStatementPDE and HeatKernelDataExistenceStatement (def … : Prop, stated not proved), heatKernelDataExistenceStatement_implies_pde, and model inhabitants including heatKernelExistenceStatementPDE_conclusion_adversarial / heatKernelDataExistenceStatement_conclusion_adversarial.

approach.conjugate_heat_bridge: ConjugateHeatBridge.lean (eighth invocation): the D7 conjugate-heat interface (ConjugateHeatSpacetime with volume, laplacian, scalarMul, backwardTimeDerivative) on the corrected domain. (1) Refutation: IsRiemannianConjugateHeatSpacetime constrains only the volume, so the two-point datum with laplacian = LinearMap.id, scalarMul = 0, backwardTimeDerivative = 0 satisfies it and □* u = -u forces K = 0 against positivity; general schema with injective Laplacian. (2) Repair: IsConjugateHeatKernelPDE (v2) = genuine HasDerivAt conjugate heat equation ∂_t K(x,y,t) = -Δ_x K(·,y,t)(x) + R(x)K(x,y,t) on t < t0, positivity/normalization/Dirac on a D12 admissible class. (3) Transport: any HeatKernelDataV1 datum maps to it by the time reversal t ↦ t0 - t (chain rule, normalization through symmetry, terminal Dirac limit through tendsto_const_sub_nhdsLT). (4) Flat model: the time-reversed D10 kernel inhabits it in every dimension on the integrable and C_c classes, is symmetric, has unit mass, conserves mass, satisfies Chapman-Kolmogorov, and refutes the legacy snapshot predicate in positive dimension (so the predicates are not equivalent). (5) Positive counterpart: FlatConjugateCorrectedDomainExistence is proved. approach.finite_pinned_operator: Ninth invocation. FiniteSpaceHeat.lean. The schematic interface is repaired in the finite setting by pinning the generator: FiniteHeatOperator = {L : Matrix X X ℝ // Lᵀ = L ∧ (∀ x, ∑ y, L x y = 0) ∧ (∀ x y, x ≠ y → 0 < L x y)}. Kernel K x y t = (exp (t • L)) x y for t > 0, clipped to 0 at t ≤ 0. Positivity: shift c = ∑ x |L x x| + 1 makes M = L + c • 1 entrywise positive; exp (t • L) = exp (-(t c)) • exp (t • M) (Matrix.exp_add_of_commute + Matrix.exp_diagonal for the scalar identity exponential); entries of exp (t • M) are nonnegative tsums and strictly positive by comparison with the n = 1 term (Summable.le_tsum). Row sums via the HasSum of the exponential series pushed through the CLM A ↦ A *ᵥ 1 (Matrix.expSeries_hasSum_exp, L *ᵥ 1 = 0, hasSum_single, HasSum.unique); column sums by symmetry. Chapman-Kolmogorov from Matrix.exp_add_of_commute. PDE: hasDerivAt_exp_smul_const' + hasDerivAt_pi twice gives HasDerivAt (fun s => exp (s • L) x y) ((L * exp (t • L)) x y) t, rewritten to the operator form via Matrix.mul_apply/mulVecLin_apply; the clipped kernel is eventually equal near t > 0. Dirac: continuity at 0 + finite-sum limits + ∫ over Measure.count = Finset sum (integral_count). Maximum principle: positivity preservation through the shifted decomposition; ℓ¹ contraction from nonnegative entries and unit column sums. Dissipativity: the discrete Dirichlet identity (expand (u x - u y)^2, use row/column sums and symmetry). Closed-Riemannian certification: counting measure + discrete metric + Finite.compactSpace. Legacy D7 datum via HeatKernelCore.toHeatKernelData with the FULL pointwise initial condition (all functions, since the space is finite). No legacy source edited.
approach.finite_uniqueness: Tenth invocation. FiniteUniqueness.lean. The energy method at the finite level: energy G u = sum x, (u x)^2; hasDerivAt_energy gives d/dt energy = 2 * sum x, u x * Delta u x for any pointwise solution of d_t u = Delta u; energy_antitoneOn uses antitoneOn_of_deriv_nonpos with the dissipativity laplacian_quadraticForm_nonpos; tendsto_energy_zero is the finite-sum limit; eq_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto_zero combines le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto (E T <= E eps for eps -> 0+) with energy_nonneg to force E = 0; eq_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto applies it to a difference with common initial limit. The Dirac limit of IsHeatKernelPDE against the singleton test functions singleFun y = indicator {y} (continuous under DiscreteTopology, integrable for count) is exactly if z=y then 1 else 0, so eq_of_pde_of_dirac gives kernel uniqueness for t > 0; eq_finiteHeatKernel_of_isHeatKernelPDE identifies every interface inhabitant with the matrix-exponential kernel; exists_unique_finiteHeatKernel is the causal existence-and-uniqueness statement. The D7 consumer Poincare.D7.HeatKernel.UniquenessStatus records the D7-level well-posedness summary.
approach.finite_conjugate_uniqueness: Tenth invocation. FiniteConjugateUniqueness.lean. Backward equations need a Grönwall weight: if -(C*E u) <= sum x, u x * A u x then the reversed function N s = u (t0-s) satisfies E' <= 2C E, so F s = exp(-(2C)s)*E(N s) is antitone; a solution with zero terminal limit vanishes (eq_zero_of_backward_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto) and two solutions with the same terminal limit coincide (eq_of_backward_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto). For the conjugate predicate, the terminal Dirac limit against singletons is the pointwise terminal data, giving IsConjugateHeatKernelPDE.eq_of_same. The canonical time-reversed kernel finiteConjugateKernel G t0 x y t = finiteHeatKernel G x y (t0-t) is anticausal, solves the conjugate equation (chain rule), is normalized (row sums + symmetry) and attains the terminal Dirac data; finite_isConjugateHeatKernelPDE inhabits the repaired predicate and exists_unique_finiteConjugateKernel is the anticausal existence-and-uniqueness statement. The D7 consumer Poincare.D7.ConjugateHeat.UniquenessStatus records the D7-level summary.
approach.conjugate_scalar_curvature: Eleventh invocation. ConjugateScalarCurvature.lean: (1) Mass law: for any finite pinned Laplace operator G and coefficient R, a pointwise solution of d_t K = -ΔK + RK has mass derivative sum x, R x * K x y t (the Laplacian term sums to zero by vanishing column sums). (2) Obstruction: the v2 predicate's normalized field makes the mass identically 1, so sum x, R x * K x y t = 0 for all t < t0; with R >= 0 positive somewhere this contradicts strict positivity, so v2 is unsatisfiable (concrete two-point complete-graph instance). (3) Repair v3 IsConjugateHeatKernelPDEMassLaw: same PDE/positivity/Dirac fields, with the unit-mass field replaced by the mass law HasDerivAt (fun s => ∫ x, K x y s) (∫ x, S.scalarMul (fun z => K z y t) x) and the terminal normalization ∫ x, K x y t → 1. (4) Existence: the curvature kernel finiteConjKernelWith G R t0 x y t = exp ((t0 - t) • (L - diag R)) x y for t < t0 and 0 for t ≥ t0 inhabits v3 for every R (shifted positive-entry decomposition for positivity: shift curvatureShift = sum |L x x - R x| + 1 makes (L - diag R) + shift • 1 entrywise positive; chain rule for the PDE, with the generator identity (A * exp (sA)) x y = Δ_x exp (sA) (·,y) - R x exp (sA) x y; terminal limit from continuity of the matrix exponential at 0). (5) Uniqueness: the Grönwall-weighted backward energy argument of FiniteConjugateUniqueness applies verbatim with the curvature bound -(sum |R|) * energy ≤ sum u * (R u); hence exists_unique_finiteConjKernelWith. (6) No loss: v2 → v3 on the finite pinned spacetime (mass law derived from the PDE; terminal normalization from the Dirac limit against the constant 1). The D7 consumer ScalarCurvatureStatus records all of it at the D7 level. Semantic class: proved theorem over the pinned finite model (with two checked refutations of the v2 field combination); not a manifold statement; R = 0 transport unchanged.
approach.finite_ergodicity: Twelfth invocation. FiniteErgodicity.lean: the Dirichlet form dirichletForm G u = (1/2) sum x sum y, L x y (u x - u y)^2 is nonnegative, equals the negative quadratic form and vanishes exactly on the constants; the variance identity sum x sum y, (u x - u y)^2 = 2 * card X * sum u^2 - 2 * (sum u)^2 makes the Poincare inequality quantitative: card X * minWeight G * energy u <= dirichletForm G u on mean-zero u, and minWeight G > 0 (strict off-diagonal positivity) gives the combinatorial Dirichlet gap card X * minWeight G. The Dirichlet form of the complete-graph operator equals card X * energy exactly, so the constant is optimal there. The pinned Laplacian annihilates constants in summed form (sum x, Delta u x = 0), so the mean of a solution is conserved; the Gronwall-weighted energy exp (2 Lambda t) * energy (u t) has derivative exp (2 Lambda t) * (2 Lambda * energy - 2 * dirichletForm) <= 0, giving energy (u T) <= energy (u eps) * exp (-(2 Lambda)(T - eps)). The equilibrium deviation x |-> K x y t - (card X)^-1 is mean-zero (unit column sums), solves the same PDE (Delta of a constant is zero) and has Dirac energy 1 - (card X)^-1 at 0+; letting eps -> 0+ gives energy (K . y T - equilibrium) <= (1 - (card X)^-1) * exp (-(2 Lambda) T), convergence of the energy to 0 at infinity for Lambda > 0, and the pointwise bound |K x y t - (card X)^-1| <= sqrt (1 - (card X)^-1) * exp (-(Lambda t)). For the complete-graph operator the closed form (card X)^-1 + exp (-(card X) t) (delta x y - (card X)^-1) satisfies the PDE and the Dirac data (uniqueness identifies it with finiteHeatKernel), and its equilibrium energy is exactly the decay bound, so the bound is attained. The D7 consumer Poincare.D7.HeatKernel.ErgodicityStatus records the gap, Poincare inequality, decay, convergence, invariance of the equilibrium state and the complete-graph sharpness. Semantic class: proved theorem over the pinned finite model (quantitative, with a sharp instance); not a manifold statement.
approach.weak_heat_equation: WeakHeatEquation.lean (thirteenth invocation). The weak (test-paired) form of the heat equation on the D12 corrected admissible-test-function domain: IsWeakHeatKernelPDE S C K := ∀ phi ∈ C, ∀ y t>0, HasDerivAt (fun s => ∫ x, phi x * K x y s) (∫ x, phi x * S.laplacian (fun z => K z y t) x) t. The transfer weakHeatKernelPDE_of_hasDerivAt takes the pointwise PDE plus WeakHeatCertificates (snapshot measurability/integrability, paired-Laplacian measurability, and laplacian_locally_bounded: ∀ y a b, 0<a → a≤b → ∃ D, ∀ x t ∈ [a,b], |ΔK| ≤ D) and applies mathlib's hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le on Ioo (t0/2) (2 t0) with dominating function (max D 0) * ‖phi‖. The certificates are proved for the D10 flat kernel: K ≤ (4πt)^(-n/2); u e^{-u} ≤ e^{-1} gives K ‖z‖²/(4t²) ≤ (4πt)^(-n/2)/(e t); rpow_neg_half_le_of_le gives prefactor monotonicity; hence |ΔK| ≤ flatLaplacianBound n a = (4πa)^(-n/2)(1/(e a)+n/(2 a)) on [a,b]. Flat instances on the integrable and C_c classes in every dimension; flat_weak_snapshot_refuted records that the weak equation holds while the snapshot predicate IsHeatKernelV1 is refuted in positive dimension. The weak equation is a strict weakening of the pointwise PDE; the converse is not claimed. The manifold-side obligation is exactly the certificate structure (Gaussian bounds for ΔK).
approach.weak_finite: WeakFinite.lean (thirteenth invocation). The weak interface on the pinned finite Markov-chain model: the certificates are proved by finite-dimensional arguments (kernel entries in [0,1] at positive times via exp_smul_le_one; |ΔK| ≤ finiteLaplacianBound G = ∑ x ∑ z |L x z| on [a,b], a>0, by the triangle inequality and the entry bound; measurability/integrability from Integrable.of_finite on a finite type with measurable singletons and finite counting measure). finite_weakHeatKernel instantiates IsWeakHeatKernelPDE via IsHeatKernelPDE.toWeak and finite_isHeatKernelPDE; finite_weak_and_pde_inhabited records the simultaneous inhabitation of both predicates. This is the second, non-flat model of the weak interface and shows the certificate proof is not tied to the Gaussian analysis.

blockers.interface_level_finding: The D7 predicate's heat-equation field is a snapshot operator identity, not the PDE and not satisfiable by the honest flat Euclidean spacetime for the D10 kernel in positive dimension (PredicateSemantics.lean). The fourth invocation supplies the checked repair candidate IsHeatKernelPDE (v2) with the genuine HasDerivAt field. The sixth invocation adds: the only sound geometric necessary condition expressible over the schematic interface is Δ1 = 0 (AnnihilatesConstants); the classical self-adjointness axiom is PROVED FALSE there for the honest 1D flat packaged Laplacian (LaplacianSymmetryRefutation.lean: u = 1, v = log cosh give ∫1·Δv = 2 ≠ 0); and the classical C_c/C² forms need a smooth normed structure the interface does not carry. blockers.statement_level_finding: The D7 predicate-level existence statements are not merely unproved: they are FALSE as formalized.
